concepts.title: Communication: Meaning, Elements and Types
concepts.definition: Communication is the sharing of meaning between a sender and a receiver through a message carried by a medium, completed by feedback. It may be verbal or non-verbal, formal or informal, and one-way or interactive -- and its success is judged by how far the intended meaning arrived intact.
concepts.key_idea: Sender, message, medium, receiver, feedback -- communication is complete only when meaning lands.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe106.txt communication sections (concept of communication, elements, verbal and non verbal, one way and two way, feedback)
question_patterns: define communication and name its elements
in class 11 media and communication technology: why is feedback important in communication
distinguish verbal from non verbal communication with examples
when is communication said to be effective
compare one way and two way communication
identify the elements in a given communication situation

solution_steps.explain: Trace sender to message to medium to receiver, then the feedback that closes the loop.
Words carry verbal meaning; gestures, tone and appearance carry non-verbal meaning alongside.
Ask whether the receiver's understanding matches the sender's intent -- that match defines effectiveness.

concepts.title: Media: Print, Electronic and New Media
concepts.definition: Media are the channels mass communication rides on: print media such as newspapers and magazines, electronic media such as radio and television, and the new digital media of internet, e-mail and social platforms. Each has reach, cost and credibility differences that shape what it is used for.
concepts.key_idea: Print endures, broadcast travels, digital interacts -- pick the medium that fits the message.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe106.txt media sections (print media newspaper magazine, radio television, internet email social media, role of media in society)
question_patterns: classify media into print electronic and new media with examples
in class 11 media and communication technology: how does the internet differ from television as a medium
what roles do media play in a democratic society
compare radio and newspaper as sources of information
why is social media called interactive media
evaluate the reliability of different media sources

solution_steps.explain: Print endures on paper, electronic broadcasts by airwaves, and new media distributes digitally over networks.
Check reach, speed, cost, permanence and interactivity -- print is permanent and reflective, broadcast is fast, digital is interactive.
Announcements, entertainment, education and discussion each suit different media choices.

concepts.title: Communication Technology in Daily and Family Life
concepts.definition: Modern tools -- telephones, computers and the internet -- have changed how families study, shop, bank, work and stay in touch, and how communities access services. The chapter also flags the discipline of use: verifying information, protecting privacy and balancing screen time with real interaction.
concepts.key_idea: Technology multiplies contact -- and demands judgment: verify, protect, balance.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe106.txt technology sections (telephone computer internet in daily life, e learning, online services, misuse and safe use, screen time)
question_patterns: how has communication technology changed family life
in class 11 media and communication technology: what precautions should guide internet use

solution_steps.explain: List the daily portals -- calls, study material, banking, shopping, news -- where technology has entered family routine.
False information, fraud and privacy loss ride the same pipes; verification and guarded personal data are the countermeasures.
Time limits and device-free hours keep technology a servant of relationships, not their replacement.

worked_examples.question_pattern: In a classroom lecture, identify sender, message, medium, receiver and feedback, and one non-verbal element.

solution_template.explain: Teacher sends, lecture content is the message, spoken words carry it, students receive.
Questions and puzzled looks tell the teacher whether to re-explain.
Tone, gestures and eye contact add meaning beyond the words.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A colony must warn residents about water supply cut tomorrow. Which medium suits best and why?

solution_template.explain: Speed and sure reach tonight matter more than depth or permanence.
Newspaper is too slow; a social media group and loudspeaker announcement reach residents tonight.
Interactive digital plus a local announcement fits the purpose -- medium matched to message.
